title: notiongit-sync run summary
description: Machine-readable summary of one notiongit-sync run. See ../docs/run-summary-schema.md for the field-by-field guide, the result/code table and example payloads.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema. 1 for every payload this document describes; bumped only for a breaking change to this shape.

result.description: Coarse, stable outcome of the run.

code.description: Specific, machine-readable reason for `result`. New codes may be added within schema_version 1 without a version bump; a consumer that sees an unrecognized code should fall back to handling it by `result` alone.

changed.description: true when any tracked file (_pages/, _posts/, _data/nav.yml, _data/home.yml, or the managed lines of _config.yml) was created, updated, renamed or deleted this run. Independent of `result`: a row_errors failure can still report changed:true if some rows succeeded before another row failed. Always false for no_op and every other failure code, where nothing was ever written.

started_at.description: UTC timestamp, ISO 8601, when this run began (before any Notion API call).

finished_at.description: UTC timestamp, ISO 8601, when this run reached its terminal state.

detail.description: Safe, human-readable, single-line detail: counts and filenames of generated files only. Never contains a Notion token, database ID, raw API response, page title/body, or stack trace — any error text that could echo one is redacted to "[redacted]" before it reaches this field.

sectionCounts.description: Counts for one database section (pages or posts), or null when that section didn't run this time — either because it aborted before finishing (missing_credentials, bulk_delete_guard, sync_error all leave both pages and posts null) or, on an otherwise-successful run, because that database simply isn't configured (a posts-only or pages-only setup leaves the other one null). A documented fallback either way, not a missing value.

dataFiles.description: Which of the three shared data/config files were rewritten this run, or null only when no section ran at all (a run that aborted before finishing any section). Whenever at least one section ran — even a posts-only run, which never touches these files — this is real data, not a fallback: it can legitimately be all-false.
